lastText: AOKLAGEBERICHTMenu19141915191619171918HARD MODE — EROSION 3/43 November 1918The Army Goes HomeThe front · 3 November 1918Expand the mapSabacLembergKraśnikRawa RuskaGoriziaViennaPrzemyślTeschenPlessBadenVilla GiustiThe armistice is signed in a villa near Padua, and the army that signed it is no longer an army. The Czechs, the Poles, the South Slavs and the Hungarians have gone home as regiments, with their weapons, to the countries that they now belong to. What is left is a staff, a number of Austrian German and Hungarian regiments in good order, and several hundred thousand prisoners. The monarchy ends as the army did: not with a battle, but because each part of it decided it had a better place to be.-10MANPOWER -4MUNITIONS -10IMPERIAL COHESION Settled recordSerbia and Galicia, 1914: the swing force sent to Galicia first. The offensive into Russian Poland: launched with the Third Army held back at the San to cover the southern flank. Rawa, September 1914: the battle broken off and the army drawn back behind the San. Serbia, autumn 1914: the advance stopped on the Kolubara. Przemyśl, 1915: relief pressed through the Carpathian winter. Przemyśl, February 1915: the fortress told that no more relief would come. Gorlice: a German commander accepted. Italy: attacked at once. Serbia, September 1915: the attack made under Mackensen. Montenegro, January 1916: the campaign opened at once.
